gaps.sentence: It was ___ best meal I've ever had.
He's always been fascinated by ___ universe.
The novel had a huge effect on ___ young people of the 1960s.
gaps.explanation: 'The young people of the 1960s' — defined by the of-phrase, so 'the'.

gaps.sentence: He was wearing ___ strange metal bracelet on his left wrist.
gaps.explanation: 'A strange bracelet' (first mention); body parts after prepositions traditionally take 'the' (on the left wrist).

gaps.sentence: ___ influenza, or flu, is highly contagious.
gaps.explanation: Most disease names take no article: influenza, flu, malaria (compare: the flu is also heard informally).

gaps.sentence: We reached ___ agreement after hours of negotiation.
gaps.explanation: 'Reach an agreement' — 'agreement' starts with a vowel sound.

gaps.sentence: ___ rich should do more to help the poor.
gaps.explanation: The + adjective = a group of people: the rich.

gaps.sentence: We bought ___ antique mirror at the flea market.
gaps.explanation: 'An antique mirror' — 'antique' starts with a vowel sound.
